answer.rationale: The 18% cost cut mandate is the binding constraint this cycle. memory_c2 documents that moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor previously cut unit cost sharply, onboarding was quick, and invoicing stayed accurate — exactly the cost reduction we need with minimal delivery risk. I want to verify that record before committing because the assembly line is already at 94% with no buffer, so any onboarding friction would be costly. The other candidate directions don't meet the objective as directly: renew_incumbent (memory_c1, memory_c4) preserves stability but the incumbent's pricing won't absorb an 18% cut; negotiate_terms could help but is unlikely to recover 18% in one cycle; add_second_source (memory_c3) addresses risk but not cost; defer_decision (memory_c5) is viable only for non-critical items, and this contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so deferral risks a supply gap at the assembly line.
